definition: Reconstructing the full 3D shape of an object from one or more images, using learned shape priors or implicit fields.
details: Reconstructing the full 3D shape of an object from one or more images, using learned shape priors or implicit fields.

explainer.lead: 3D object reconstruction turns one or more flat images into a complete three-dimensional object shape. It matters because a single view leaves parts hidden, so the method must combine visible evidence with learned knowledge about plausible shapes.

tiers.eli5: You see one or two photos of a chair and work out what the whole chair looks like from every side, including the parts the photos never showed.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers feed one or a few views into a learned shape prior or an implicit field to get a dense mesh or occupancy volume. A common pitfall is trusting output for unobserved sides, where the prior invents plausible but wrong geometry.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, a model learns a mapping from image observations to a 3D representation, often an implicit field f(x) whose zero level set defines the surface, trained against shape priors. Limits: ambiguity from sparse views and dependence on the prior's coverage.

explainer.example: Given one photograph of a mug, a reconstruction system can model the visible rim and body, then use learned mug shapes to infer the unseen back and the hidden portion of the handle. The result is a complete 3D mug, although the inferred surfaces may differ from the real mug.
explainer.intuition: An image supplies direct evidence for visible surfaces and indirect clues about the rest of an object. Learned shape priors use patterns from previous examples to propose a complete shape, while implicit fields describe that shape as a continuous function over 3D space.
howItWorks: Provide one image or several images of the object.
Extract visual features that describe its visible shape.
Use learned shape knowledge to infer a complete 3D structure, including hidden parts.
Represent the result with an implicit field or another 3D shape representation.
Sample or convert that representation for display, measurement, or further processing.
explainer.whyItMatters: It bridges ordinary 2D images and 3D representations without requiring every surface to be directly visible. It also makes the distinction between observed geometry and inferred geometry important when judging reliability.
misconceptions: A complete reconstruction is not necessarily an exact recovery of hidden surfaces.
An implicit field is a way to represent 3D shape, not a photograph with added depth.
